hook: The SHSAT *CRASHED*. Here's what counts now.
dek: SHSAT tech problems sent students home Saturday, here's who gets a retest and what's next.

slides.label: The Glitch
slides.text: Saturday, Nov. 14: the SHSAT platform *froze, crashed or never loaded* for thousands of 8th graders.

slides.label: The Scale
slides.text: The Post reports about *2,500 students* were stopped mid-test, with Brooklyn Tech and Stuyvesant among the sites hit.

slides.label: The Fix
slides.text: NYC Public Schools says affected students get a *new test date automatically*, no re-registration needed.

slides.label: Does It Count
slides.text: The DOE says testing on a new date *will not hurt your score* or your shot at a specialized high school.

slides.label: Finished Anyway
slides.text: Students who completed Saturday's test can *choose to retake it* if they feel the glitch hurt their performance.

slides.label: The Timeline
slides.text: Gothamist reports updates by Monday, Nov. 16. A DOE letter says new dates come by *Nov. 20*.

slides.label: Accountability
slides.text: Elected officials are demanding answers, saying *'accountability cannot be outsourced'* to vendor Pearson.

slides.label: Why It Matters
slides.text: The SHSAT is the *sole factor* for admission to 8 of NYC's 9 specialized high schools, offers go out by score.

cta_line: Let them *rest*. Watch for that date.

caption_instagram:
The SHSAT retest glitch left thousands of NYC eighth graders staring at frozen screens Saturday, Nov. 14, right in the middle of the test they'd been grinding toward for months.

NYC Public Schools says the technical failure, caused by testing vendor Pearson, means affected students get a new test date automatically, no re-registration needed, and testing on a new date will not hurt their score or their shot at a specialized high school. Students who finished anyway can choose to retake it too.

Elected officials are already pushing for a full investigation, saying accountability cannot be outsourced to a vendor. Families are still waiting on the actual makeup date, promised by Nov. 20.

caption_linkedin:
New York City just ran a live case study in what happens when a 17 million dollar ed tech contract meets exam day pressure. Saturday's SHSAT, now fully computer adaptive, went down when the testing platform from vendor Pearson failed, freezing or crashing the exam for thousands of eighth graders at sites including Brooklyn Tech and Stuyvesant.

NYC Public Schools moved fast on the public facing promise: automatic reschedule, no score penalty, retake option for students who finished. But elected officials are asking the harder question, the one every operator should sit with: accountability cannot be outsourced. When you hand a high stakes, high volume process to a third party vendor, the contract does not transfer the responsibility, it just adds a layer between you and the people depending on the system working.

For founders building anything adaptive, anything high stakes, anything with a deadline nobody chose, what's your plan for the day the platform fails?
#EdTech #SystemsReliability #NYCSchools
